task.description: Review src/design/iss0105-gbl084-raw-guard-scoping.md against docs/issues/ISS-0105.json. This design proposes an IN-PLACE EDIT to migrations/GBL-084_rls_removal.sql (unusual — GBL-102 and GBL-103 both deliberately avoided in-place edits to GBL-084 for the gated-migration-runner path, citing 'migrations don't re-run once recorded'). The design's justification: GBL-084's file is read fresh from disk by tests/integration/test_iss503_rls_removal.zig's readGbl084Sql() on every test run, with no applied-tracking for that specific re-execution — so an in-place edit takes effect immediately for the test, without needing to touch the gated path (which GBL-102/103 already independently handle). Verify this reasoning is actually sound: (1) confirm readGbl084Sql() really does read from disk fresh every call, not from any cache, (2) confirm editing GBL-084's guard clause in place does NOT break anything about the gated migration-runner path — specifically, does the gated path's Migrations.run() ever re-read GBL-084's file content after it's already recorded as applied, in a way that an in-place edit could cause unexpected re-execution or a checksum/hash mismatch error? Check src/db/migrations.zig for any content-hash verification against already-applied migrations (some migration runners store a checksum and error if a previously-applied file's content changes) — if such a check exists, an in-place edit would BREAK every environment where GBL-084 is already recorded as applied, which would be a serious regression. (3) Verify TC-ISS503-01's fixture slug ('iss503-<suffix>' per the design) is genuinely not tc-prefixed and not exempted by the new scoping, by reading the actual test source yourself. (4) Verify TC-ISS503-02/03 are genuinely unaffected. (5) Confirm the exact guard SQL matches GBL-102/103's established pattern.
acceptance_criteria: PASS or FAIL verdict with specific issues if FAIL

result.summary: src/design/iss0105-gbl084-raw-guard-scoping.md validated against ISS-0105/#363. The design's core claim -- that in-place editing migrations/GBL-084_rls_removal.sql's guard clause is safe despite GBL-102/GBL-103 having deliberately avoided in-place edits -- was independently re-derived from source, not accepted on the design's word. src/db/migrations.zig was read in full: its applied-migration skip logic (line 210, `if (applied.contains(filename)) continue;`) is a pure filename lookup against public.schema_migrations, whose schema (lines 108-113) stores only schema_name, version, and applied_at -- no content-hash, checksum, or byte-comparison column exists anywhere in the file or in the schema_migrations DDL. There is no mechanism by which an in-place edit to an already-applied migration's file content could raise an error or trigger unexpected re-execution on the gated path; the runner simply keeps skipping the filename exactly as before, unconditionally. This is the single most important check per the acceptance criteria and it clears the design of BLOCKER risk on Mechanism A (the gated path). readGbl084Sql() (lines 92-113 of tests/integration/test_iss503_rls_removal.zig) was confirmed to open the migrations directory and call dir.readFileAlloc() fresh on every invocation, with no static/cache variable, called independently at lines 259, 339, and 393 by TC-ISS503-01/02/03 respectively -- so the in-place edit takes effect on Mechanism B (the raw re-execution path) exactly as the design claims. TC-ISS503-01's createTenantRow() (lines 117-133) was read directly: its slug is 'iss503-{suffix}' (not tc-% prefixed) and tenant_type is omitted from the INSERT column list, taking the schema default 'production' per GBL-080_env01_tenant_type_field.sql line 21 -- both new guard conditions (tenant_type = 'production' AND slug NOT LIKE 'tc-%') evaluate TRUE for this fixture, so the guard still fires and TC-ISS503-01 is unaffected. TC-ISS503-02/03 were read directly: both issue their own unscoped, table-wide UPDATE public.tenant SET storage_mode = 'SCHEMA' WHERE storage_mode = 'LEGACY_RLS' before re-running the guard, which flips every LEGACY_RLS row (scoped-exempt or not) to SCHEMA first -- so v_legacy_count is 0 under the new scoped WHERE clause regardless of scoping, since a scoped subset of an already-empty set is trivially empty. Both tests' pass-path assertions are unaffected. The proposed guard SQL (`AND tenant_type = 'production' AND slug NOT LIKE 'tc-%'`) is byte-identical to GBL-103_iss0100_guard_tc_slug_scope.sql lines 48-50, the established pattern. No implementation code beyond the single illustrative SQL diff is present in the design; scope is correctly limited to migrations/GBL-084_rls_removal.sql (1 file); dependencies and no-regression claims against GBL-102/GBL-103/lint_test_isolation.py/iss107 test are addressed in §7 with specific verification. All coverage, completeness, correctness, and security checklist items pass.
